question: Fed decisions (Jun-Sep)
resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds rate. The decisions on the target federal funds rate are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: June 16-17; July 28-29; and September 15-16.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

"Other" means any option not listed here.
research:
I couldn't open the July 29 statement or the June 17 statement on the Fed's site. The June and July holds below come from secondary sources that agree with each other and with the Fed's rate-change table.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-08-26: The Fed's open-market page shows the last change on 2025-12-11, a 25 bp cut to **3.50%-3.75%**, so the upper bound is 3.75%. It lists no changes from January through August 2026. [Fed open market](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm)
- The scored decisions are in the FOMC statements: June 17, July 29 and September 16, 2026. [Fed calendar](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-06-17: **Pause.** The FOMC held at 3.50%-3.75% in Warsh's first meeting as chair. The vote was unanimous, and the shorter statement dropped the easing bias. [KPMG](https://www.kpmg.com/us/en/articles/2026/june-2026-fomc-meeting.html), [MetalsMine](https://www.metalsmine.com/calendar/4-us-fomc-statement)
- 2026-07-29: **Pause.** The FOMC held at 3.50%-3.75% on a 9-3 vote. Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissented in favor of a 25 bp **hike**. [PCBB](https://www.pcbb.com/industry-insights/economy/2026-07-29-fomc-july-2026), [Star-Advertiser](https://www.staradvertiser.com/2026/07/29/breaking-news/fed-holds-rates-steady-as-3-policymakers-dissent-in-favor-of-hike/), [Fed implementation note](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/files/monetary20260729a1.pdf)
- **This settles part of the question.** The first two results are Pause-Pause, so every option that starts with "Cut" is ruled out. Only three outcomes are left, all decided by September 16:
  - a hold resolves **Pause-Pause-Pause**;
  - a cut resolves **Pause-Pause-Cut**;
  - a hike resolves **"Other"**, since the rules put any hike there.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08 (early August, per the URL date): a headline reported Warsh was "open to September rate hike". I couldn't open it (403 error). [roic.ai](https://www.roic.ai/news/warsh-open-to-september-rate-hike-08-06-2026)
- 2026-07-30: After the July hold, a Reuters-sourced report said markets put about **57%** on a September hike, down from almost 100% before the meeting. [BusinessToday](https://www.businesstoday.com.my/2026/07/30/fed-holds-rates-steady-as-markets-cut-september-hike-expectations/)
- 2026-07-29: U.S. stocks fell after the decision. A summary said markets priced two 25 bp hikes in 2026. [ifyouspent](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/fed-decision-recap-july-2026)
- 2026-06-17: In the June dot plot, 9 of 18 officials projected at least one hike in 2026, which analysts called hawkish. [AlphaMaven](https://www.alpha-maven.com/story/crypto/kevin-warsh-holds-interest-rates-steady-in-first-policy-meeting-as-fed-chair-crypto-briefing), [Trustnet](https://www.trustnet.com/news/13478711/fed-holds-rates-at-warshs-first-meeting-while-hawkish-dot-plot-divides-analyst-opinion), [MNI](https://www.mnimarkets.com/articles/mni-fed-review-jun-2026-jumping-past-neutral-to-hawkish-1781728747352)
- Inflation backdrop: reports cite CPI at about 3.4% year over year and the Fed's preferred PCE measure at about 3.7%, both through July and well above the 2% target. I couldn't confirm when those figures were published.

## 4. Base rates
- The Fed has now held at five straight meetings since the December 2025 cut, counting July. [ifyouspent](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/fed-decision-recap-july-2026)
- In past cycles, a long hold that ends with hawkish dissents, as here, has more often turned into a hike than a cut. Three dissents is unusual. More than two at one meeting has been rare since the 1990s.
- I found no source in 2026 arguing for a near-term cut. Policy talk is about holding versus hiking.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-07-29: Kalshi priced a July hold at 76% and a hike at 24%. A September-hike market traded at about **44% Yes / 56% No**. [Pythia newsletter](https://pythia.beehiiv.com/p/new-post-23b5)
- About 2026-07-30: market pricing (Reuters-sourced) put a September hike at about 57%. [BusinessToday](https://www.businesstoday.com.my/2026/07/30/fed-holds-rates-steady-as-markets-cut-september-hike-expectations/)
- An undated article cites Kalshi at 57% for a September hike to 3.75%-4.00%. [tech-insider](https://tech-insider.org/polymarket-fed-september-2026-rate-odds/)
- I found no current Polymarket or Kalshi price for this exact combination question. Pricing for a September **cut** looks negligible in every source I found.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Late August: the Jackson Hole symposium with Warsh's speech. It's a key signal for whether the Fed holds or hikes.
- Late August: July PCE inflation release.
- Early September: August jobs report.
- About September 10-11: August CPI. One calendar lists a September 11 CPI release.
- September 15-16: FOMC meeting, statement and new projections. This decides between Pause-Pause-Pause, Pause-Pause-Cut and "Other".
